And His words: and when I restrained the Children of Israel from you, when you came to them with clear proofs, and those of them who disbelieved said: this is nothing but plain sorcery, that is: and remember My favour upon you in My restraining them from you when you came to them with the proofs and decisive arguments for your prophethood and your messengership from God to them, and they denied you and accused you of being a sorcerer, and strove to kill you and crucify you; then I delivered you from them, raised you up to Myself, purified you from their defilement and sufficed you against their evil. This indicates that this bestowal of favour was from God to him after his being raised to the lowest heaven, or else that this bestowal of favour takes place on the Day of Resurrection and is expressed in the past tense to indicate that it will inevitably occur. This is among the secrets of the unseen which God disclosed to His Messenger Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).

And His words: and when I inspired the disciples: believe in Me and in My messenger (5:111): this too is among the favours bestowed upon him (peace be upon him), in that He made for him companions and helpers. Then it was said: what is meant by this inspiration (waḥy) is the inspiration of instilling (ilhām), as He said: And We inspired the mother of Moses: suckle him, to the end of the verse (28:7), and this is the inspiration of instilling, without dispute; and as He Exalted said: And your Lord inspired the bee: take for yourself dwellings in the mountains and in the trees and in what they build. Then eat of all fruits and follow the ways of your Lord made smooth, to the end of the verse (16:68-69). Thus some of the early authorities (salaf) said about this verse: and when I inspired the disciples: believe in Me and in My messenger. They said: We believe, that is, in God and in the Messenger of God, and bear witness that we are Muslims, that is: they were instilled with that, and they complied with what they had been instilled.
Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: God, Mighty and Majestic, instilled that in them. Al-Suddī said: He cast that into their hearts.

It is also possible that what is meant is: and when I inspired them through your mediation, so that you called them to faith in God and in His Messenger, and they responded to you, submitted and followed you, and said: We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims.

This is the story of the Table, and after it the sūrah is named, so that it is called "Sūrat al-Māʾidah" (the Sūrah of the Table). It is among the favours God bestowed upon His servant and messenger Jesus (peace be upon him), when He answered his supplication by sending it down; so God sent it down as a sign, a dazzling miraculous proof and a decisive argument.
Some of the leading scholars have mentioned that the story of the Table is not mentioned in the Gospel, and that the Christians know of it only from the Muslims; and God knows best.

So His words, Exalted: When the disciples said, and they are the followers of Jesus (peace be upon him): O Jesus son of Mary, can your Lord (5:112). This is the reading of many, while others read hal tastaṭīʿu rabbaka, "can you ask your Lord"{{fn:The reading of al-Kisāʾī, with the second-person verb and rabbaka in the accusative, in place of the majority reading hal yastaṭīʿu rabbuka.}}, that is: are you able to ask your Lord to send down to us a table from heaven?

The table (māʾidah) is a tray on which there is food. Some of them mentioned that they asked for that only because of their need and poverty, so they asked that a table be sent down to them every day from which they might feed themselves and strengthen themselves for worship.

He said: Fear God, if you are believers, that is: the Messiah (peace be upon him) answered them, saying to them: Fear God, and do not ask for this, for it may be a trial for you; and rely upon God in seeking provision, if you are believers.

They said: We wish to eat from it (5:113), that is: we are in need of eating from it, and that our hearts be at rest when we witness it coming down as provision for us from heaven, and that we may know that you have told us the truth, that is: and that we may increase in faith in you and in knowledge of your messengership, and that we may be among the witnesses to it, that is: and that we may bear witness that it is a sign from God and a proof and argument for your prophethood and the truth of what you have brought.

Jesus son of Mary said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, that it may be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us (5:114). Al-Suddī said: that is, that we may take the day on which it came down as a festival which we and those after us hold in honour. Sufyān al-Thawrī said: meaning a day on which we pray. Qatādah said: they wanted it to be for their posterity after them. And from Salmān al-Fārisī: an admonition for us and for those after us. And it was said: sufficient for the first of us and the last of us.

and a sign from You, that is: a proof which You set up of Your power over all things and of Your answering my supplication, so that they believe me in what I convey from You; and provide for us, that is: from Yourself, a pleasant provision without toil or weariness; and You are the best of providers. God said: I shall send it down to you; but whoever of you disbelieves afterwards (5:115), that is: whoever of your community, O Jesus, denies it and stubbornly rejects it, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I shall not punish anyone among the worlds, that is: among the people of your time, like His words: and on the Day the Hour comes: admit the people of Pharaoh to the severest punishment (40:46), and like His words: Truly the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire (4:145).

Ibn Jarīr related, by way of ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī, from Abū al-Mughīrah al-Qawwās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection will be three: the hypocrites, those of the people of the Table who disbelieved, and the people of Pharaoh.
### Mention of the reports related from the early authorities on the descent of the Table upon the disciples

Abū Jaʿfar ibn Jarīr said: al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Layth, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he used to relate of Jesus son of Mary that he said to the Children of Israel: Are you willing to fast for God thirty days, then ask Him and He will give you what you ask? For the wage of the worker is owed by the one for whom he works. So they did so, then said: O teacher of goodness, you told us that the wage of the worker is owed by the one for whom he works, and you commanded us to fast thirty days, and we did so; and we never worked thirty days for anyone without his feeding us food when we finished. So can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven? Jesus said: Fear God, if you are believers. They said: We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts be at rest, and that we may know that you have told us the truth, and that we may be among the witnesses to it. Jesus son of Mary said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, that it may be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You; and provide for us, and You are the best of providers. God said: I shall send it down to you; but whoever of you disbelieves afterwards, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I shall not punish anyone among the worlds (5:112-115). He said: Then the angels came flying with a table from heaven, on which were seven fish and seven loaves, until they set it down before them, and the last of the people ate from it as the first of them had eaten.

So Ibn Jarīr related it. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related it from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Ibn Wahb, from al-Layth, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās used to relate, and he mentioned the like of it.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also said: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam related to us: Abū Zurʿah Wahb Allāh ibn Rāshid related to us: ʿUqayl ibn Khālid related to us that Ibn Shihāb informed him, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that they said to Jesus son of Mary: Pray to God to send down to us a table from heaven. He said: So the angels came down carrying a table, on which were seven fish and seven loaves, and the last of the people ate from it as the first of them had eaten.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: my father related to us: al-Ḥasan ibn Qazaʿah al-Bāhilī related to us: Sufyān ibn Ḥabīb related to us: Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah related to us, from Qatādah, from Khilās, from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "The Table came down from heaven with bread and meat on it, and they were commanded not to be unfaithful and not to put any aside for the morrow; but they were unfaithful, stored it up and put it aside, and so they were transformed into apes and swine."

Ibn Jarīr related it likewise from al-Ḥasan ibn Qazaʿah. Then Ibn Jarīr related it from Ibn Bashshār, from Ibn Abī ʿAdī, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Khilās, from ʿAmmār, who said: The Table came down with fruit of the fruits of Paradise on it, and they were commanded not to be unfaithful, not to hide any and not to store any up. He said: But the people were unfaithful, hid some and stored some up, and so God transformed them into apes and swine.

Ibn Jarīr said: Ibn al-Muthannā related to us: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Dāwūd related to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from a man of the Banū ʿIjl, who said: I prayed beside ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, and when he finished he said: Do you know how the affair of the Table of the Children of Israel was? He said: I said: No. He said: They asked Jesus son of Mary for a table on which there would be food from which they could eat and which would not run out. He said: So it was said to them: It will remain with you so long as you do not hide any, or act unfaithfully, or put any aside; but if you do, I shall punish you with a punishment with which I shall not punish anyone among the worlds. He said: And their day had not passed before they hid some, put some aside and acted unfaithfully, and so they were punished with a punishment with which no one among the worlds has been punished. And you, O company of Arabs, used to follow the tails of camels and sheep; then God sent among you a messenger from among yourselves, whose lineage and descent you know, and he informed you that you will prevail over the non-Arabs, and he forbade you to hoard gold and silver. By God, night and day will not pass away before you hoard them both, and God punishes you with a painful punishment.

And he said: al-Qāsim related to us: Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Abū Maʿshar, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that the Table came down upon Jesus son of Mary with seven loaves and seven fish on it, and they ate from it as they wished. He said: Then some of them stole from it, saying: "Perhaps it will not come down tomorrow." So it was taken up.

Al-ʿAwfī said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: There came down upon Jesus son of Mary and the disciples a tray on which were bread and fish, from which they ate wherever they alighted, whenever they wished. Khaṣīf said, from ʿIkrimah and Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Table was a fish and loaves. Mujāhid said: It was food that used to come down upon them wherever they alighted. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī said: The Table came down as bread and fish. ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfī said: The Table was fish in which was the taste of everything.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He sent it down from heaven upon the Children of Israel, and every day there used to come down to them on that Table some of the fruits of Paradise, and they ate what they wished of various kinds. Four thousand would sit at it, and when they had eaten God replaced it with the like of it for others like them. They remained in that state for as long as God, Mighty and Majestic, willed.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He sent down to them a loaf of barley and fish, and God filled their folds with blessing, so that a group would eat and then go out, and then others would come and eat and then go out, until all of them had eaten and there was still some left over.
Al-Aʿmash said, from Muslim, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: Everything was sent down on it except meat.

Sufyān al-Thawrī said, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Zādhān and Maysarah; and Jarīr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Maysarah, who said: When the Table was set before the Children of Israel, hands reached across it for every kind of food except meat.
And from ʿIkrimah: The bread of the Table was of rice. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related it.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAlī informed us in what he wrote to me: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways related to us: Abū ʿAbd Allāh ʿAbd al-Quddūs ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mirdās al-ʿAbdarī, the client of the Banū ʿAbd al-Dār, related to me, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, from Salmān al-Khayr, that he said: When the disciples asked Jesus son of Mary for the Table, he disliked that intensely and said: Be content with what God has provided you on the earth, and do not ask for the Table from heaven; for if it comes down to you it will be a sign from your Lord, and Thamūd perished only when they asked their prophet for a sign, and were tried by it until their destruction lay in it. But they refused anything but that he should bring it to them, and that is why they said: We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts be at rest, to the end of the verse.

When Jesus saw that they would accept nothing but that he should pray to Him for it on their behalf, he rose, cast off his wool, put on black hair-cloth, a cloak of hair and a mantle of hair, then performed the ablution and the full washing, entered his place of prayer and prayed as long as God willed. When he had completed his prayer he stood upright facing the direction of prayer (qiblah), set his feet in line until they were even, pressed heel to heel and aligned the toes, placed his right hand upon his left over his chest, lowered his gaze and bowed his head in humility; then he let his eyes flow with weeping, and his tears kept streaming down his cheeks and dripping from the ends of his beard until the ground before his face was wet from his humility. When he saw that, he called upon God and said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven. So God sent down to them a red cloth between two clouds, one cloud above it and one cloud below it, while they looked at it in the air plunging down from the sphere of heaven and descending towards them, and Jesus wept in fear of the conditions God had laid upon them in it, namely that He would punish whoever of them disbelieved in it after its descent with a punishment with which He had punished no one among the worlds; and he was praying to God from his place, saying: O God, make it a mercy; my God, do not make it a punishment; my God, how many a wonder have I asked of You and You have given me; my God, make us thankful to You; my God, I seek refuge in You lest You should have sent it down in anger and as a requital; my God, make it safety and well-being, and do not make it a trial and an exemplary punishment.

He kept on praying until the cloth settled before Jesus, with the disciples and his companions around him, and they smelt a sweet fragrance the like of which they had never smelt before. Jesus and the disciples fell down prostrate to God in thanks for His having provided for them from where they had not reckoned and shown them in it a mighty sign full of wonder and admonition. The Jews came to look, and saw a wondrous thing which left them with grief and distress; then they went away in intense rage. Jesus, the disciples and his companions came forward until they sat around the cloth, and behold, there was a napkin covering it. Jesus said: Who among us is the boldest to uncover the napkin from this cloth, the most confident of himself, and the best of us in his record with his Lord? Let him uncover this sign so that we may see it, praise our Lord, make mention of His name, and eat of His provision which He has provided us. The disciples said: O Spirit of God and His Word, you are the most entitled of us to that, and the most deserving of us to uncover it. So Jesus (peace be upon him) rose, performed a fresh ablution, then entered his place of prayer and likewise prayed some units of prayer, then wept for a long time and prayed to God to permit him to uncover it and to place in it blessing and provision for him and for his people. Then he went and sat down at the cloth, took hold of the napkin and said: "In the name of God, the best of providers," and uncovered the cloth, and behold, on it was a huge roasted fish, with no scales on it and no bones inside it, with fat flowing from it in a stream; around it were arranged herbs of every kind except leeks; at its head was vinegar and at its tail salt; and around the herbs were five loaves, on one of which were olives, on another dates, and on another five pomegranates.

Simon (Shamʿūn), the chief of the disciples, said to Jesus: O Spirit of God and His Word, is this of the food of this world or of the food of Paradise? He said: Is it not time for you to take warning from the signs you see and desist from prying into questions? How I fear for you that you will be punished on account of the sending down of this sign! Simon said: By the God of Israel, I did not intend by it a questioning, O son of the truthful woman. Jesus (peace be upon him) said: Nothing of what you see is of the food of Paradise or of the food of this world; it is only something God originated in the air by the supreme, overpowering power, saying to it: Be, and it was, quicker than the twinkling of an eye. So eat of what you asked for, in the name of God, and praise your Lord for it, and He will supply you more of it and increase you, for He is the Originator, the Powerful, the Appreciative.

They said: O Spirit of God and His Word, we would like you to show us a sign within this sign. Jesus said: Glory be to God! Were you not satisfied with what you have seen in this sign, that you should ask for another sign within it? Then Jesus (peace be upon him) turned to the fish and said: O fish, return by God's leave to life as you were. So God brought it to life by His power, and it quivered and returned by God's leave to being alive and fresh, licking its lips as a lion licks its lips, its eyes rolling and gleaming, and its scales came back upon it. The people were terrified of it and drew back. When Jesus saw that from them he said: What is the matter with you, that you ask for a sign, and when your Lord shows it to you, you dislike it? How I fear for you that you will be punished for what you do! O fish, return by God's leave to what you were. And it returned by God's leave to being roasted, as it had been in its first created state.

They said to Jesus: Be you the one, O Spirit of God, who begins eating from it, and then we after you. Jesus said: God forbid that! Let him begin eating who asked for it. When the disciples and their companions saw their prophet's refusal of it, they feared that its descent might be a mark of wrath and that in eating of it there might be exemplary punishment, so they kept away from it. When Jesus saw that, he summoned to it the poor and the chronically ill, and said: Eat of the provision of your Lord and the prayer of your prophet, and praise God who has sent it down for you; its wholesomeness will be yours, and its punishment upon others than you. Begin your eating in the name of God, and end it with praise of God. So they did, and one thousand three hundred persons, men and women, ate from it, each one of them turning away from it full and belching. Jesus and the disciples looked, and behold, what was on it was just as it had been when it was sent down from heaven, with nothing of it diminished. Then it was raised up to heaven while they looked on, and every poor person who had eaten from it became rich, and every chronically ill person who had eaten from it was healed, and they remained rich and healthy until they departed from this world.

The disciples and their companions who had refused to eat from it repented with such regret that their eyelashes ran with tears, and the grief of it remained in their hearts until the day of their death. He said: After that, whenever the Table came down, the Children of Israel came hurrying to it from every place, jostling one another, the rich and the poor, the young and the old, the healthy and the sick, climbing over one another. When He saw that, He made it come by turns, descending one day and not descending the next. They remained in that state for forty days, with it descending to them every other day when the forenoon had risen high, and it would remain set out and eaten from until, when they rose, it was lifted away from them by God's leave into the air of the sky, while they watched its shadow on the ground until it disappeared from them.

He said: Then God revealed to His prophet Jesus (peace be upon him): Make My provision, the Table, for the orphans, the poor and the chronically ill, to the exclusion of the rich among the people. When he did that, the rich among the people grew suspicious of it and resented that, until they doubted it within themselves and made the people doubt it, and spread abroad foul and evil talk about it. Satan gained from them what he wanted and cast his whispering into the hearts of the doubters, until they said to Jesus: Tell us about the Table and its descent from heaven, is it true? For many people among us have come to doubt it. Jesus (peace be upon him) said: You are ruined, by the God of the Messiah! You asked your prophet for the Table, that he should ask your Lord for it on your behalf, and when he did so, and He sent it down to you as a mercy and a provision and showed you in it signs and lessons, you denied it and doubted it. So receive the tidings of punishment, for it is coming down upon you unless God has mercy on you.

And God revealed to Jesus: I shall take the deniers according to My condition, for I shall punish whoever of them disbelieves in the Table after its descent with a punishment with which I shall not punish anyone among the worlds. He said: When evening came upon those who doubted it, and they took to their beds in the finest of forms with their wives, feeling secure, then in the last part of the night God transformed them into swine, and in the morning they were following after filth in the rubbish heaps.

This is a very strange report. Ibn Abī Ḥātim split it up in several places in this story, and I have gathered it together for him so that its narrative may be fuller and more complete; and God, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.

All these reports indicate that the Table came down upon the Children of Israel in the days of Jesus son of Mary, as an answer from God to his supplication, and as is indicated by the apparent sense of this passage of the Mighty Qurʾān: God said: I shall send it down to you, to the end of the verse.

Some have said that it did not come down. Layth ibn Abī Sulaym related, from Mujāhid, concerning His words send down to us a table from heaven, that he said: It is a parable that was set forth, and nothing came down.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Jarīr related it. Then Ibn Jarīr said: al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Qāsim, that is, Ibn Sallām, related to us: Ḥajjāj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, who said: A table on which was food; they refused it when the punishment was presented to them should they disbelieve, so they refused that it should come down upon them.
He also said: Ibn al-Muthannā related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Manṣūr ibn Zādhān, from al-Ḥasan, that he said of the Table: It did not come down.

And Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, who said: al-Ḥasan used to say: When it was said to them, but whoever of you disbelieves afterwards, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I shall not punish anyone among the worlds, they said: We have no need of it; so it did not come down.

These are sound chains of transmission (asānīd) to Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan, and that may be strengthened by the fact that the Christians do not know the report of the Table and it is not in their book; had it come down, that would have been among the things there are abundant motives to transmit, and it would have been found in their book by mass transmission (mutawātir), or at the very least by single reports (āḥād); and God knows best. But the view held by the majority is that it did come down, and that is what Ibn Jarīr chose. He said: because He Exalted informed of its descent in His words, Exalted: I shall send it down to you; but whoever of you disbelieves afterwards, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I shall not punish anyone among the worlds. He said: and God's promise and His threat are true and truthful.

This view is, and God knows best, the correct one, as the reports and traditions from the early authorities and others indicate. The historians have mentioned that Mūsā ibn Nuṣayr, the deputy of the Umayyads in the conquests of the lands of the Maghrib, found the Table there, studded with pearls and various kinds of jewels, and sent it to the Commander of the Faithful al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, the builder of the congregational mosque of Damascus; but he died while it was on the way, and it was carried to his brother Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, the caliph after him, and the people saw it and marvelled at it greatly because of the precious rubies and peerless jewels in it. It is said that this table belonged to Solomon son of David (peace be upon them both); and God knows best.

Imām Aḥmad said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥakam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Quraysh said to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): Pray to your Lord for us to make al-Ṣafā gold for us, and we shall believe in you. He said: "And will you do so?" They said: Yes. He said: So he prayed, and Gabriel came to him and said: Your Lord sends you greetings of peace and says to you: If you wish, al-Ṣafā will become gold for them, but whoever of them disbelieves after that, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I shall not punish anyone among the worlds; and if you wish, I shall open for them the door of repentance and mercy. He said: "Rather, the door of repentance and mercy."
Then Aḥmad, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Ḥākim in his Mustadrak related it from the ḥadīth of Sufyān al-Thawrī, with it.

This too is among what God Exalted will address to His servant and messenger Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him), saying to him on the Day of Resurrection, in the presence of those who took him and his mother as two gods besides God: And when God said: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to people: take me and my mother as two gods besides God? (5:116). This is a threat to the Christians, and a rebuke and reproach of them before the assembled witnesses. So said Qatādah and others, and Qatādah adduced as evidence for that His words, Exalted: This is the Day when the truthful will profit from their truthfulness (5:119).
Al-Suddī said: this address and the reply took place in this world.
Ibn Jarīr said: this is the correct view, and that was when God raised him to the lowest heaven. Ibn Jarīr argued for that on two grounds:
- The first: that the speech is in the past tense.
- The second: His words if You punish them and if You forgive them (5:118).

These two proofs are open to question, because many of the affairs of the Day of Resurrection are mentioned in the past tense, to indicate their occurrence and certainty. And the meaning of His words if You punish them, they are Your servants, to the end of the verse, is disavowal of them and referral of the will concerning them to God, and making that dependent on a condition does not require that it occur, as in the parallel cases among the verses.

What Qatādah and others said is the more evident view, and God knows best: that this will take place on the Day of Resurrection, to indicate the threatening of the Christians and the reproaching and rebuking of them before the assembled witnesses on the Day of Resurrection. A ḥadīth traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ) has been related to this effect, related by the ḥadīth master (ḥāfiẓ) Ibn ʿAsākir in the biographical entry on Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the client of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who was reliable, who said: I heard Abū Burdah relate to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz from his father Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the prophets and their communities will be summoned; then Jesus will be summoned, and God will remind him of His favour upon him, and he will acknowledge it, and He will say: O Jesus son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother, to the end of the verse (5:110). Then He will say: Did you say to people: take me and my mother as two gods besides God? And he will deny having said that. Then the Christians will be brought and questioned, and they will say: Yes, he commanded us to do that. He said: Then the hair of Jesus (peace be upon him) will be made long, and every angel among the angels will take hold of a hair of the hair of his head and his body, and he will make them kneel before God, Mighty and Majestic, for the span of a thousand years, until the proof is established against them, the cross is raised up for them, and they are led off to the Fire." This is a strange and rare ḥadīth.

And His words: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to: this is a granting of success in observing proper courtesy in the perfect reply, as Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: my father related to us: Ibn Abī ʿUmar related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿAmr, from Ṭāwūs, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: Jesus will be taught his argument, and God taught it to him, in His words: And when God said: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to people: take me and my mother as two gods besides God? Abū Hurayrah said, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): So God taught him: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to, to the end of the verse.
Al-Thawrī related it, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from Ṭāwūs, in similar words.

And His words: If I had said it, You would have known it, that is: had this issued from me, You would have known it, O my Lord, for nothing is hidden from You of what I have said or intended within myself or harboured. That is why he said: You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Your Self; truly You are the Knower of the unseen things. I did not say to them anything except what You commanded me to convey: worship God, my Lord and your Lord (5:117), that is: I called them only to that with which You sent me and commanded me to convey: worship God, my Lord and your Lord, that is: this is what I said to them; and I was a witness over them as long as I was among them, that is: I used to witness their deeds while I was in their midst; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things.

Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī said: Shuʿbah related to us, saying: Sufyān al-Thawrī and I went to al-Mughīrah ibn al-Nuʿmān, and he dictated it to Sufyān while I was with him, and when he rose I copied it from Sufyān. So he related to us, saying: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr relate from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood among us with an admonition and said: "O people, you will be gathered to God, Mighty and Majestic, barefoot, naked and uncircumcised: as We began the first creation, We shall repeat it (21:104). The first of creatures to be clothed will be Abraham. Behold, men of my community will be brought and taken off to the left, and I shall say: My companions! And it will be said: You do not know what they innovated after you. So I shall say as the righteous servant said: and I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things. If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, truly You are the Mighty, the Wise (5:117-118). And it will be said: These never ceased turning back on their heels since you parted from them."
Al-Bukhārī related it at this verse from al-Walīd, from Abū Shuʿbah, and from Muḥammad ibn Kathīr, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, both of them from al-Mughīrah ibn al-Nuʿmān, with it.

And His words: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, truly You are the Mighty, the Wise (5:118): this speech contains the referral of the will to God, Mighty and Majestic, for He is the Doer of what He wills, who is not questioned about what He does while they are questioned. And it contains disavowal of the Christians who lied against God and against His messenger and assigned to God a rival, a consort and a child; exalted is God far above what they say. This verse has a great importance and a wondrous import, and it has come in the ḥadīth that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood in prayer with it one night until morning, repeating it.

Imām Aḥmad said: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl related to us: Fulayt al-ʿĀmirī related to me, from Jasrah al-ʿĀmiriyyah, from Abū Dharr (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed one night and recited a single verse until morning came, bowing with it and prostrating with it: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, truly You are the Mighty, the Wise. When morning came I said: O Messenger of God, you kept on reciting this verse until morning, bowing with it and prostrating with it? He said: "I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for intercession for my community, and He granted it to me; and it will be attained, God willing, by whoever does not associate anything with God."

Another route and another wording: Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā related to us: Qudāmah ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us: Jasrah bint Dajājah related to me that she set out to perform the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah) and came to al-Rabadhah, where she heard Abū Dharr say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood one night for the evening prayer and led the people in prayer; then some of his companions stayed behind praying. When he saw them standing and staying behind, he went off to his quarters, and when he saw that the people had left the place empty he returned to his place and prayed. I came and stood behind him, and he motioned to me with his right hand, so I stood on his right. Then Ibn Masʿūd came and stood behind me and behind him, and he motioned to him with his left hand, so he stood on his left. So the three of us stood, each of us praying by himself and reciting of the Qurʾān whatever God willed that he recite. And he stood with one verse of the Qurʾān, repeating it until he prayed the dawn prayer. When morning came I motioned to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ask him what he intended by what he did last night. Ibn Masʿūd said with his hand: I shall not ask him about anything until he speaks to me. So I said: May my father and mother be your ransom, you stood with a single verse of the Qurʾān when you have the whole Qurʾān; had one of us done this we would have found fault with him. He said: "I prayed for my community." I said: And what answer were you given? Or: what reply was returned to you? He said: "I was answered with that which, if many of them were to catch a glimpse of it, they would abandon the prayer." I said: Shall I not give the people the good news? He said: "Yes." So I set off at a brisk pace, and had gone about a stone's throw, when ʿUmar said: O Messenger of God, if you send this to the people they will shrink from worship. So he called to him to come back, and he came back. And that verse was: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, truly You are the Mighty, the Wise.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me that Bakr ibn Sawādah related to him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) recited the words of Jesus: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, truly You are the Mighty, the Wise, then raised his hands and said: "O God, my community!" and wept. So God said: O Gabriel, go to Muḥammad, though your Lord knows best, and ask him what makes him weep. Gabriel came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) told him what he had said. So God said: O Gabriel, go to Muḥammad and say: We shall please you concerning your community and shall not grieve you.

Imām Aḥmad said: Ḥasan related to us: Ibn Lahīʿah related to us: Ibn Hubayrah related to us that he heard Abū Tamīm al-Jayshānī say: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab related to me: I heard Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was absent from us one day and did not come out, until we thought he would never come out. When he came out he prostrated with a prostration so long that we thought his soul had been taken in it. When he raised his head he said: "My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, consulted me about my community: what shall I do with them? I said: Whatever You will, O my Lord; they are Your creation and Your servants. He consulted me a second time, and I said the same to Him. Then He said: I shall not disgrace you in your community, O Muḥammad. And He gave me the good news that the first of my community to enter Paradise with me will be seventy thousand, with every thousand another seventy thousand, upon whom there is no reckoning. Then He sent to me, saying: Supplicate and you will be answered; ask and you will be given." So I said to His messenger: Will my Lord grant me my request? He said: He has not sent me to you except to grant you. "My Lord has indeed given me, and there is no boasting in it: He has forgiven me my past sins and those to come while I walk about alive and well; He has granted me that my community will not starve and will not be overcome; He has given me al-Kawthar, which is a river in Paradise that flows into my Basin; He has given me might, victory, and terror running a month's journey ahead of my community; He has granted me that I shall be the first of the prophets to enter Paradise; He has made the spoils of war lawful and wholesome for me and my community; He has made lawful for us much of what was made severe upon those before us; and He has not placed upon us any hardship in religion."

God Exalted says, in answer to His servant and messenger Jesus son of Mary, regarding what he had conveyed to Him of his disavowal of the heretical Christians who lie against God and against His messenger, and of his referring the will concerning them to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic; at that point He Exalted says: This is the Day when the truthful will profit from their truthfulness (5:119).
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who says: the Day when those who affirm God's oneness will profit from their affirmation of His oneness.

For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, that is: dwelling in them, neither changing nor passing away; God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, as He Exalted said: and good pleasure from God is greater (9:72).
What relates to that verse in the way of ḥadīth will come later.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related here a ḥadīth, saying: Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to us: al-Muḥāribī related to us, from Layth, from ʿUthmān, meaning Ibn ʿUmayr Abū al-Yaqẓān, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Then the Lord Exalted will manifest Himself to them and say: Ask of Me, ask of Me, and I shall give you." He said: "So they will ask Him for His good pleasure, and He will say: My good pleasure is that I settle you in My abode and grant you My honour; so ask of Me and I shall give you. So they will ask Him for His good pleasure." He said: "Then He will make them witness that He is pleased with them."

And His words: That is the great triumph, that is: this is the great success, than which there is nothing greater, as He Exalted said: For the like of this let the workers work (37:61), and as He said: and for this let the competitors compete (83:26).

And His words: To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He has power over all things (5:120), that is: He is the Creator of all things, their Owner, the One who disposes of them and has power over them; all of them are His possession, under His subjugation and His power and within His will. So He has no peer, no vizier, no equal, no father, no child and no consort; there is no god other than Him and no lord besides Him.
Ibn Wahb said: I heard Ḥuyayy ibn ʿAbd Allāh relate, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The last sūrah to be sent down was Sūrat al-Māʾidah.

When the Exalted had related the story of Zachariah (peace be upon him), and how He brought forth from him, in his old age and with his wife barren, a child pure, clean and blessed, He followed it by relating the story of Mary and His bringing forth from her her son Jesus (peace be upon them both) without a father; for between the two stories there is a correspondence and a resemblance. For this reason He mentioned them together in Āl ʿImrān, here, and in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ, joining the two stories because of the closeness in meaning between them, so as to show His servants His power and the greatness of His authority, and that He has power over whatever He wills. So He said: And mention in the Book Mary (19:16). She is Mary daughter of ʿImrān, of the line of David (peace be upon him), and she was of a pure and goodly house among the Children of Israel. God, Exalted, has related the story of her mother giving birth to her in Āl ʿImrān: that she vowed her as one consecrated (muḥarrarah), that is, to serve the sanctuary of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), for they used to draw near to God by that; so her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance and made her grow with a goodly growth (3:37). She grew up among the Children of Israel in a magnificent manner, and became one of the devout worshipping women renowned for great worship, devotion and unflagging effort. She was in the guardianship of her sister's husband (and it was said: her maternal aunt's husband) Zachariah, the prophet of the Children of Israel at that time and their great one, to whom they referred in matters of their religion. Zachariah saw in her such astonishing marks of divine favour (karāmāt) as dazzled him: Whenever Zachariah entered upon her in the sanctuary he found provision with her. He said: O Mary, whence have you this? She said: It is from God; indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning (3:37). It is related that he would find with her the fruit of winter in summer and the fruit of summer in winter, as was explained earlier in Āl ʿImrān. So when God, Exalted, and His is the wisdom and the conclusive argument, willed to bring forth from her His servant and messenger Jesus (peace be upon him), one of the five great messengers of firm resolve (ulū al-ʿazm), she withdrew from her people to an eastern place (19:16), that is, she went apart from them and drew aside from them, and went to the east of the sacred sanctuary.

Al-Suddī said: because of a menstruation that came upon her. And it was said: for some other reason. Abū Kudaynah said, from Qābūs ibn Abī Ẓibyān, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Prayer towards the House and pilgrimage to it were prescribed for the People of the Book, and nothing turned them away from it except the saying of your Lord: she withdrew from her people to an eastern place (19:16). He said: Mary went out to an eastern place, so they prayed towards the rising-place of the sun. Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Jarīr related it.

Ibn Jarīr also said: Isḥāq ibn Shāhīn related to us: Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿĀmir, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I am indeed the most knowledgeable of God's creatures as to why the Christians took the east as their direction of prayer (qiblah): it is because of the words of God, Exalted, she withdrew from her people to an eastern place (19:16); and they took the birthplace of Jesus as a qiblah.
Qatādah said: an eastern place (19:16): remote and set apart.
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: She went with her pitcher to draw water.
Nawf al-Bikālī said: She took for herself a dwelling in which to devote herself to worship. And God knows best.

His words: and she took a veil apart from them (19:17), that is, she screened herself from them and hid herself. Then God, Exalted, sent to her Gabriel (peace be upon him), and he appeared to her in the likeness of a well-formed man (19:17), that is, in the form of a complete and perfect human being.
Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Qatādah, Ibn Jurayj, Wahb ibn Munabbih and al-Suddī said regarding His words So We sent to her Our Spirit (19:17): meaning Gabriel (peace be upon him).

What they said is the apparent sense of the Qurʾān, for the Exalted has said in the other verse: The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down upon your heart, that you might be one of the warners (26:193-194).

Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī said, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The spirit of Jesus (peace be upon him) was among the spirits from which the covenant was taken in the time of Adam, and it was he who appeared to her in the likeness of a well-formed man (that is, the spirit of Jesus) and she conceived the one who addressed her, and he entered into her mouth.
This is extremely strange and objectionable, and it seems to be an Israelite tradition (Isrāʾīliyyāt).

She said: I seek refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing (19:18), that is, when the angel appeared to her in the form of a man, while she was in a secluded place with a veil between her and her people, she was afraid of him and thought that he wanted her for himself, so she said: I seek refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing (19:18), that is, if you fear God. This was a reminder to him of God, and this is what is prescribed in repelling an assailant: that it be by the gentlest means, then the next gentlest. So she first sought to make him fear God, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Jarīr said: Abū Kurayb related to me: Abū Bakr related to us, from ʿĀṣim, who said: Abū Wāʾil said, and he mentioned the story of Mary, and said: She knew that the God-fearing man is one possessed of restraint, when she said: I seek refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing. He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord (19:18-19), that is, the angel said to her, answering her and removing the fear for herself that had arisen in her: I am not what you think; rather I am a messenger of your Lord, that is, He has sent me to you. And it is said that when she mentioned the All-Merciful, Gabriel trembled with fear and returned to his own form, and said: "I am only a messenger of your Lord, that He may grant you (li-yahaba laki) a pure boy."

Thus did Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, one of the famous reciters, read it. The others read: that I may grant you (li-ahaba laki) a pure boy (19:19).{{fn:Two canonical readings (qirāʾāt) of 19:19: li-yahaba, "that He may grant", with God as the subject, and li-ahaba, "that I may grant", with the angel speaking as God's instrument.}} Both readings have a sound basis and a correct meaning, and each entails the other.

She said: How can I have a boy, when no man has touched me, and I have not been unchaste? (19:20), that is, Mary marvelled at this and said: How can I have a boy? That is, in what manner could this boy come to be from me, when I have no husband, and no indecency can be imagined of me? Hence she said: when no man has touched me, and I have not been unchaste (19:20). The baghiyy is the fornicatress; hence it comes in the ḥadīth that the hire of the prostitute (mahr al-baghiyy) was forbidden.

He said: So it will be. Your Lord has said: It is easy for Me (19:21), that is, the angel said to her, answering what she had asked: God has said that a boy will indeed come to be from you, even though you have no husband and no indecency has come from you, for He has power over whatever He wills. Hence He said: and that We may make him a sign for mankind (19:21), that is, a proof and a token for mankind of the power of their Maker and Creator, who has diversified their creation: He created their father Adam from neither male nor female; He created Eve from a male without a female; He created the rest of the progeny from male and female, except Jesus, for He brought him into being from a female without a male. Thus the fourfold division was completed, pointing to the perfection of His power and the greatness of His authority; so there is no god other than He and no Lord besides Him.

His words: and a mercy from Us (19:21), that is, and We shall make this boy a mercy from God, a prophet among the prophets, calling to the worship of God, Exalted, and His oneness, as the Exalted said in the other verse: When the angels said: O Mary, indeed God gives you glad tidings of a Word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, eminent in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near. And he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be among the righteous (3:45-46), that is, he will call to the worship of God his Lord in his cradle and in his maturity.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: my father related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Ibrāhīm, Duḥaym, related to us: Marwān related to us: al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥārith al-Kūfī related to us, from Mujāhid, who said: Mary (peace be upon her) said: When I was alone, Jesus would talk to me and speak with me while he was in my womb, and when I was among people he would glorify God and magnify Him in my womb.

His words: and it was a matter decreed (19:21). It may be that this is part of Gabriel's speech to Mary, informing her that this is a matter foreordained in the knowledge of God, Exalted, His decree and His will. And it may be that it is part of God's report, Exalted, to His Messenger Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him), and that He alluded by this to the breathing into her private part, as the Exalted said: And Mary daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it of Our Spirit (66:12), and He said: And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit (21:91).

Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: and it was a matter decreed (19:21), that is, God had resolved upon this, and there was no escaping it. Ibn Jarīr also preferred this in his commentary, and related no other view. And God knows best.

The Exalted says, informing about Mary, that when Gabriel had said to her from God, Exalted, what he said, she submitted to the decree of God, Exalted. More than one of the scholars of the early generations (salaf) mentioned that at that point the angel, that is, Gabriel (peace be upon him), breathed into the opening of her garment, and the breath descended until it entered the private part, and she conceived the child by the leave of God, Exalted. When she had conceived him she was sorely distressed by it and did not know what she would say to people, for she knew that people would not believe her in what she told them; however, she disclosed her secret and mentioned her situation to her sister, the wife of Zachariah. That was because Zachariah (peace be upon him) had asked God for a child and had been granted that, and his wife had conceived. Mary went in to her, and she rose to her and embraced her, and said: Have you perceived, O Mary, that I am pregnant? Mary said to her: And have you also come to know that I am pregnant? And she told her of her situation and what had befallen her, and they were a household of faith and belief. Thereafter, whenever the wife of Zachariah came face to face with Mary, she would feel the one in her womb prostrating to the one in Mary's belly, that is, honouring him and humbling himself before him; for prostration at greeting was lawful in their religious community (millah), just as Joseph's parents and brothers prostrated to him, and just as God commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam (peace be upon him). But it was forbidden in this religious community of ours, to perfect the veneration of the majesty of the Lord, Exalted.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us, saying: It was read out to al-Ḥārith ibn Miskīn while I was listening; he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim informed us, saying: Mālik (may God have mercy on him) said: It has reached me that Jesus son of Mary and John son of Zachariah were the sons of two sisters, and that they were both carried in the womb at the same time; and it has reached me that the mother of John said to Mary: I feel that what is in my belly is prostrating to what is in your belly. Mālik said: I consider that to be on account of the superiority of Jesus (peace be upon him), because God made him bring the dead to life and heal the one born blind and the leper.

Then the commentators differed regarding the duration of the pregnancy with Jesus (peace be upon him). What is well known from the majority is that she carried him for nine months. ʿIkrimah said: eight months, and he said: that is why no child born at eight months survives.

Ibn Jurayj said: al-Mughīrah ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Thaqafī informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās, when he was asked about the pregnancy of Mary, say: It was no more than that she conceived and gave birth.

This is strange, and it seems that he took it from the apparent sense of the words of the Exalted: So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place. Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree (19:22-23). But the fāʾ (the connective "then"), although it denotes immediate succession, denotes in each case the succession proper to that thing, as the Exalted said: And We certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a drop in a firm lodging. Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, and We made the clot into a lump, and We made the lump into bones (23:12-14): this fāʾ denotes the succession proper to it, and it is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs that between each two of these stages there are forty days. And the Exalted said: Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and then the earth becomes green? (22:63). So the well-known and apparent view, and God has power over all things, is that she carried him as women carry their children. Hence, when the signs of pregnancy appeared upon her, there was with her in the sanctuary a righteous man among her relatives who served the Holy House alongside her, called Joseph the Carpenter (Yūsuf al-Najjār). When he saw the heaviness and size of her belly, he found that objectionable in her; but then what he knew of her innocence, her integrity, her religion and her devotion turned him from it. Then he reflected on the condition she was in, and her situation kept going round in his mind, and he could not drive it from himself. So he brought himself to speak to her by way of allusion, and said: O Mary, I am going to ask you about a matter, so do not be hasty with me. She said: And what is it? He said: Can there ever be a tree without seed? And can there be a crop without sowing? And can there be a child without a father? She said: Yes, for she understood what he was alluding to. As for your saying, "Can there be a tree without seed, and a crop without sowing?": God created the tree and the crop, when He first created them, without seed and without sowing. "And can there be a creature without a father?": God created Adam without a father or a mother. So he believed her and accepted her condition.

When Mary sensed from her people that they suspected her of impropriety, she withdrew from them to a remote place, that is, a place distant from them and far away from them, so that she would not see them and they would not see her.

Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: When she had conceived him, filled her pitcher and returned, her menses ceased, and there befell her what befalls a woman pregnant with child by way of sickness, cravings and change of complexion, to the point that her tongue became cracked. There had never come upon any household what came upon the family of Zachariah. The talk spread among the Children of Israel, and they said: "Her companion is none other than Joseph", for there was no one with her in the temple (kanīsah) besides him. She hid herself from people and took a veil apart from them, so that no one saw her and she saw no one.

His words: Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree (19:23), that is, the labour pains compelled her and forced her to take refuge at the trunk of the palm tree, which was a palm tree in the place to which she had withdrawn.
They differed concerning it. Al-Suddī said: It was to the east of her prayer-niche (miḥrāb) in which she used to pray, in Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis).

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: She went off in flight, and when she was between Syria (al-Shām) and the land of Egypt, the labour pains struck her. And in another report from Wahb: That was eight miles from Jerusalem, in a village there called Bethlehem (Bayt Laḥm).

I say: It has already been mentioned in the ḥadīth of the Night Journey (al-Isrāʾ), in the narration of al-Nasāʾī from Anas (may God be pleased with him) and of al-Bayhaqī from Shaddād ibn Aws (may God be pleased with him), that this was in Bethlehem. And God knows best. This is the well-known account that people have received one from another, and the Christians do not doubt that it was in Bethlehem; people have received it, and the ḥadīth has come concerning it, if it is sound.

His words, Exalted, informing about her: She said: Would that I had died before this and been a thing forgotten, out of mind! (19:23). In this is proof that it is permissible to wish for death at a time of trial (fitnah), for she knew that she would be tried and tested by this newborn, regarding whom people would not take her case in a sound light nor believe her account; and after having been in their eyes a devout worshipper, she would become in their eyes, as they supposed, a harlot and fornicatress. So she said: Would that I had died before this (19:23), that is, before this state of affairs, and been a thing forgotten, out of mind (19:23), that is, had never been created and had never been anything. Ibn ʿAbbās said this.

Al-Suddī said: She said, while in the throes of labour from the pregnancy, out of shame before people: Would that I had died before this distress I am in, and this grief at my giving birth to a child without a husband; and been a thing forgotten, out of mind (19:23): forgotten, so that the search for it was abandoned, like menstrual rags which, when thrown away and discarded, are neither sought nor remembered. Likewise everything that is forgotten and abandoned is nasiyy.
Qatādah said: and been a thing forgotten, out of mind (19:23), that is, something unknown and unmentioned, so that no one would know who I am.
Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: and been a thing forgotten, out of mind (19:23): it is the miscarried foetus.
Ibn Zayd said: Had never been anything at all.

We have already presented the ḥadīths indicating the prohibition of wishing for death except at a time of trial, in connection with His words: Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous (12:101).

Some read man taḥtahā ("the one who was beneath her"), in the sense of "he who was below her"; others read min taḥtihā ("from beneath her"), taking it as a preposition.{{fn:Two readings of 19:24: man taḥtahā, making "the one beneath her" the subject who called, and min taḥtihā, "from beneath her", the reading of the majority.}}

The commentators differed as to who is intended by that. Al-ʿAwfī and others said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: Then he called to her from beneath her (19:24): Gabriel; and Jesus did not speak until she brought him to her people. Likewise Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, al-Suddī and Qatādah said: It was the angel Gabriel (blessings and peace be upon him), that is, he called to her from the lower part of the valley.

Mujāhid said: Then he called to her from beneath her (19:24): he said: Jesus son of Mary. Likewise ʿAbd al-Razzāq said, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, who said: al-Ḥasan said: It was her son. This is one of the two reports from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: that it was her son; he said: Have you not heard God say: So she pointed to him (19:29)? Ibn Zayd preferred this, as did Ibn Jarīr in his commentary.

His words: Do not grieve (19:24), that is, he called to her saying: Do not grieve. Your Lord has placed beneath you a rivulet (sariyy) (19:24). Sufyān al-Thawrī and Shuʿbah said, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib: Your Lord has placed beneath you a rivulet (19:24): he said: the brook. Likewise ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: the sariyy is the river. ʿAmr ibn Maymūn held the same: a river from which she could drink.
Mujāhid said: It is "river" in Syriac.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: The sariyy is "the small river" in Nabataean.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It is "the small river" in Syriac.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: It is the small river.
Qatādah said: It is the brook, in the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz.
Wahb ibn Munabbih said: The sariyy is a running stream of water.
Al-Suddī said: It is the river. Ibn Jarīr preferred this view. A ḥadīth traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ) has come concerning this. Al-Ṭabarānī said:

Abū Shuʿayb al-Ḥarrānī related to us: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Bābluttī related to us: Ayyūb ibn Nahīk related to us: I heard ʿIkrimah, the client (mawlā) of Ibn ʿAbbās, say: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "The sariyy of which God said to Mary, Your Lord has placed beneath you a rivulet (19:24), is a river that God brought forth for her to drink from." This is a very strange (gharīb) ḥadīth by this route. This Ayyūb ibn Nahīk is al-Ḥubulī; Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī said of him: weak. Abū Zurʿah said: objectionable in ḥadīth (munkar al-ḥadīth). Abū al-Fatḥ al-Azdī said: abandoned in ḥadīth (matrūk al-ḥadīth).

Others said: What is meant by the sariyy is Jesus (peace be upon him). This was held by al-Ḥasan, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād ibn Jaʿfar; it is one of the two reports from Qatādah, and the view of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. The first view is more apparent, and for this reason He said after it: And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree (19:25), that is, take hold of the trunk of the palm tree and draw it towards you. It was said: it was dry; Ibn ʿAbbās said this. And it was said: fruit-bearing. Mujāhid said: it was an ʿajwah palm.{{fn:ʿAjwah is a prized variety of date, especially associated with Medina.}} Al-Thawrī said, from Abū Dāwūd Nufayʿ al-Aʿmā: it was a ṣarafānah palm.{{fn:Ṣarafānah is a variety of date palm bearing hard, dense dates.}}

What is apparent is that it was a tree, but it was not in the season of its fruit; Wahb ibn Munabbih said this. For this reason He bestowed this favour upon her, in that He placed food and drink with her, and said: it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates. So eat and drink and be comforted (19:25-26), that is, be of good cheer. Hence ʿAmr ibn Maymūn said: There is nothing better for a woman in childbed than dried dates and fresh ripe dates; then he recited this noble verse.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us: Shaybān related to us: Masrūr ibn Saʿīd al-Tamīmī related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Awzāʿī related to us, from ʿUrwah ibn Ruwaym, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Honour your paternal aunt the palm tree, for it was created from the clay from which Adam (peace be upon him) was created, and there is no tree that is pollinated except it." And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Feed your women who have given birth fresh ripe dates, and if there are no fresh ripe dates then dried dates; and among trees there is no tree more honoured with God than the tree beneath which Mary daughter of ʿImrān alighted."
This is a very objectionable (munkar) ḥadīth. Abū Yaʿlā related it from Shaybān with the same chain.

Some read His words "tassāqaṭ" with doubling of the sīn, and others with it light ("tasāqaṭ"). Abū Nahīk read: tusāqiṭ upon you fresh ripe dates (19:25). Abū Isḥāq related from al-Barāʾ that he read it "tusāqiṭ", that is, with the trunk as its subject.{{fn:The variant readings of 19:25 differ in the form of the verb "drop": tassāqaṭ and tasāqaṭ (the palm tree lets fall), tusāqiṭ (causative), and, in the reading ascribed to al-Barāʾ, the masculine form with the trunk (jidhʿ) as subject.}} All of them are close in meaning.

His words: And if you see any human being (19:26), that is, whomever you may see of anyone, say: I have vowed a fast to the All-Merciful, so I shall not speak today to any human (19:26). What is meant by this "saying" is indicating it to him by gesture, not that what is meant is verbal speech, lest it contradict so I shall not speak today to any human (19:26).

Anas ibn Mālik said regarding His words I have vowed a fast to the All-Merciful (19:26): that is, silence. Likewise Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said. And in another report from Anas: "a fast and silence"; and likewise Qatādah and others besides them said.
What is meant is that when they fasted according to their law, food and speech were forbidden to them. Al-Suddī, Qatādah and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd stated this explicitly.

Abū Isḥāq said, from Ḥārithah, who said: I was with Ibn Masʿūd when two men came; one of them gave the greeting of peace and the other did not. He said: What is the matter with you? His companions said: He has sworn not to speak to people today. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: Speak to people and greet them with peace, for that was only a woman who knew that no one would believe her that she had conceived without a husband, meaning by that Mary (peace be upon her), so that it might be an excuse for her when she was questioned. Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Jarīr (may God have mercy on them both) related it.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd said: When Jesus said to Mary, Do not grieve (19:24), she said: And how should I not grieve, when you are with me, and I am neither a married woman nor a slave-girl? What excuse have I before people? Would that I had died before this and been a thing forgotten, out of mind! Jesus said to her: I will spare you the speaking: And if you see any human being, say: I have vowed a fast to the All-Merciful, so I shall not speak today to any human (19:26). He said: All of this is the speech of Jesus to his mother. And Wahb said likewise.

The Exalted says, informing about Mary, when she was commanded to fast that day of hers and not to speak to any human being, for her affair would be taken care of and her proof established: she submitted to the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, and resigned herself to His decree, and took her child, and she brought him to her people, carrying him (19:27). When they saw her thus, they considered her deed enormous and found it exceedingly objectionable, and said: O Mary, you have indeed brought a monstrous thing (fariyy) (19:27), that is, an enormous matter. Mujāhid, Qatādah, al-Suddī and more than one other said this.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: my father related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ziyād related to us: Sayyār related to us: Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān related to us: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī related to us, from Nawf al-Bikālī, who said: Her people went out in search of her, and she was of a house of prophethood and nobility, but they found no trace of her. They came upon a cowherd and said: Have you seen a young woman of such-and-such a description? He said: No, but last night I saw from my cattle something I had never seen from them before. They said: And what did you see? He said: I saw them prostrating towards this valley. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ziyād said: And I recall from Sayyār that he said: I saw a radiant light. So they set out in the direction he had told them, and Mary came to meet them; when she saw them she sat down and took her son in her lap, and they came and stood over her. They said: O Mary, you have indeed brought a monstrous thing (19:27), an enormous matter. O sister of Aaron (19:28), that is, O you who resemble Aaron in worship; your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste (19:28), that is, you are of a goodly, pure house, known for righteousness, worship and asceticism; so how did this come forth from you?

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah and al-Suddī said: It was said to her, O sister of Aaron (19:28), that is, the brother of Moses, for she was of his line, just as one says to a man of Tamīm, "O brother of Tamīm", and to a man of Muḍar, "O brother of Muḍar".
And it was said: she was ascribed to a righteous man among them whose name was Aaron, for she was compared to him in worship and asceticism.
Ibn Jarīr related from some of them that they likened her to a profligate man among them called Aaron. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related it from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.
Stranger than all of this is what Ibn Abī Ḥātim related:

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Hisinjānī related to us: Ibn Abī Maryam related to us: al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Faḍālah related to us: Abū Ṣakhr related to us, from al-Quraẓī, regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic, O sister of Aaron (19:28); he said: She was the sister of Aaron by his father and mother, and she was the sister of Moses, the brother of Aaron, who followed the track of Moses, and she watched him from a distance while they did not perceive (28:11).

This view is sheer error, for God, Exalted, has mentioned in His Book that He sent Jesus following in the footsteps of the messengers, which indicates that he was the last of the prophets to be sent, and there is none after him except Muḥammad (God's blessings and peace be upon him). Hence it is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī, from Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), that he said: "I am the closest of people to the son of Mary, for there is no prophet between me and him." Were the matter as Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī claimed, Jesus would not have been the last of the messengers save Muḥammad; rather he would have been before Solomon and David, for God has mentioned that David was after Moses (peace be upon them both), in the words of the Exalted: Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs: Send us a king and we will fight in the way of God. He said: Would you perhaps refrain from fighting if fighting were prescribed for you? They said: And why should we not fight in the way of God? (2:246), and He related the story until He said: And David killed Goliath (2:251), to the end of the verse. What emboldened al-Quraẓī to this statement is what is in the Torah after the exodus of Moses and the Children of Israel from the sea and the drowning of Pharaoh and his people, where it says: And Mary daughter of ʿImrān, the sister of the two prophets Moses and Aaron, took up the tambourine, she and the women with her, glorifying God and thanking Him for what He had bestowed upon the Children of Israel.{{fn:Exodus 15:20-21, where Miriam the sister of Aaron leads the women with timbrels.}} So al-Quraẓī believed that this was the mother of Jesus. This is a slip and a grievous error; rather, she bore the same name as this one, for they used to name after their prophets and righteous ones, as Imām Aḥmad said:

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs related to us: I heard my father mention it from Simāk, from ʿAlqamah ibn Wāʾil, from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sent me to Najrān, and they said: What do you make of what you recite, O sister of Aaron (19:28), when Moses was before Jesus by such-and-such a span? He said: So I returned and mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he said: "Why did you not tell them that they used to take names after the prophets and righteous ones who were before them?"

Muslim alone of the two Ṣaḥīḥs transmitted it, as did al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī, from the ḥadīth of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs, from his father, from Simāk, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhī said: ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb; we do not know it except from the ḥadīth of Ibn Idrīs.

Ibn Jarīr said: Yaʿqūb related to me: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Ṣadaqah, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said: I was informed that Kaʿb said: His words O sister of Aaron (19:28) do not refer to Aaron the brother of Moses. He said: ʿĀʾishah said to him: You have lied. He said: O Mother of the Believers, if the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said it, then he knows best and is best informed; otherwise, I find between the two of them six hundred years. He said: So she fell silent. There is some doubt about this chronology.

Ibn Jarīr also said: Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, regarding His words O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste (19:28); he said: She was of a house known for righteousness and not known for corruption. Among people there are those who are known for righteousness and beget offspring in it, and others who are known for corruption and beget offspring in it. Aaron was a righteous man, beloved among his clan; he is not Aaron the brother of Moses, but another Aaron. He said: And it was mentioned to us that on the day he died forty thousand of the Children of Israel, all of them named Aaron, followed his funeral procession.

His words: So she pointed to him. They said: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? (19:29), that is, when they had become suspicious of her situation and found her case objectionable, and said to her what they said, insinuating accusation against her and charging her with the slander, and she was fasting and silent that day, she referred the speech to him, and indicated to them that they should address him and speak to him. So they said, mocking her, and thinking that she was holding them in contempt and making sport of them: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? (19:29)

Maymūn ibn Mihrān said: So she pointed to him (19:29): she said: Speak to him. They said: On top of the calamity she has brought upon us, she commands us to speak to one who is in the cradle, a child!
Al-Suddī said: When she pointed to him they became angry and said: Her mockery of us, in commanding us to speak to this child, is harder on us than her fornication.

They said: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? (19:29), that is, one who is present in his cradle in the state of his childhood and infancy, how can he speak? He said: I am the servant of God (19:30). The first thing he spoke was to declare the transcendence of his Lord, Exalted, and to exonerate God from having a child, and to affirm for himself servanthood to his Lord.
His words: He has given me the Book and made me a prophet (19:30): an exoneration of his mother from the indecency that had been attributed to her.

Nawf al-Bikālī said: When they said to his mother what they said, he was suckling at her breast, so he withdrew the breast from his mouth, leaned on his left side, and said: I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet (19:30), down to His words as long as I live (19:31).

Ḥammād ibn Salamah said, from Thābit al-Bunānī: He raised his forefinger above his shoulder as he said: I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet (19:30), to the end of the verse.
ʿIkrimah said: He has given me the Book (19:30), that is, He decreed that He would give me the Book, in what He decreed.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: my father related to us: Muḥammad ibn al-Muṣaffā related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd related to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ziyād, from Anas ibn Mālik (may God be pleased with him), who said: Jesus son of Mary had studied the Gospel and mastered it in his mother's womb; and that is His saying: I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet (19:30).
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-ʿAṭṭār al-Ḥimṣī is abandoned (matrūk).

His words: And He has made me blessed wherever I may be (19:31). Mujāhid, ʿAmr ibn Qays and al-Thawrī said: And He has made me a teacher of good. And in another report from Mujāhid: greatly beneficial.

Ibn Jarīr said: Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār related to me: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd ibn Khunays al-Makhzūmī related to us: I heard Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, the client of Banū Makhzūm, say: A learned man met a learned man who was above him in knowledge, and said to him: May God have mercy on you; what of my works should I make public? He said: Commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong, for it is the religion of God with which He sent His prophets to His servants. The jurists are agreed upon the words of God, And He has made me blessed wherever I may be (19:31); and it was asked: What was his blessing? He said: Commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong, wherever he was.

His words: and He has enjoined upon me prayer and almsgiving as long as I live (19:31), are like the words of the Exalted to Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him): And worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you (15:99).

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim said, from Mālik ibn Anas, regarding His words and He has enjoined upon me prayer and almsgiving as long as I live (19:31); he said: He informed him of what would be of his affair until he died. How firmly this establishes the case against the partisans of free will (ahl al-qadar)!{{fn:The Qadariyyah, who denied that human actions are foreordained by God; Mālik's point is that Jesus was told in his cradle what he would do until his death.}}

His words: and dutiful to my mother (19:32), that is, and He commanded me to be dutiful to my mother. He mentioned it after obedience to God his Lord, because God, Exalted, very often joins the command to worship Him with obedience to parents, as the Exalted said: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and kindness to parents (17:23), and He said: Give thanks to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final return (31:14).

His words: and He has not made me a tyrant, wretched (19:32), that is, He has not made me a tyrant, arrogantly disdaining His worship and obedience and dutifulness to my mother, so that I should become wretched thereby.
Sufyān al-Thawrī said: The wretched tyrant is the one who gives himself over to anger.

One of the early generations said: You will not find anyone undutiful to his parents without finding him a wretched tyrant; then he recited: and dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a tyrant, wretched (19:32). He said: And you will not find anyone who mistreats those under his authority without finding him conceited and boastful; then he recited: and those whom your right hands possess; indeed God does not love anyone who is conceited and boastful (4:36).
