Qatādah said: It was mentioned to us that a woman saw the son of Mary bringing the dead to life and healing the one born blind and the leper, among the signs over which God had given him power and in which He had given him permission, and she said: Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breast at which you were suckled! The prophet of God Jesus (peace be upon him) said in reply to her: Blessed is he who recites the word of God and follows what is in it, and is not a tyrant, wretched.

His words: And peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised up alive (19:33): an affirmation on his part of his servanthood to God, Mighty and Majestic, and that he is a creature among the creatures of God, who lives and dies and is raised up like the rest of created beings; but he has safety in these states, which are the most arduous that servants face. God's blessings and peace be upon him.

He, Exalted, says to His Messenger Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him): that which We have related to you of the account of Jesus is the word of truth concerning which they are in doubt (19:34), that is: concerning which the followers of falsehood and the followers of truth differ, those who believe in him and those who disbelieve in him. For this reason the majority read “qawlu al-ḥaqq” with the nominative on “qawl”, while ʿĀṣim and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read qawla al-ḥaqq (with the accusative).{{fn:With the nominative the phrase is a predicate, “That is Jesus son of Mary: the word of truth…”; with the accusative it is read as an emphatic complement, “I say the word of truth”.}}

It is related of Ibn Masʿūd that he read: “That is Jesus son of Mary; he spoke the truth” (qāla al-ḥaqqa). The nominative is the more evident in point of grammatical analysis (iʿrāb), and His words, Exalted, bear witness to it: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters (3:59–60).

And when He, Exalted, had mentioned that He created him a servant and a prophet, He declared His Holy Self free of all blemish and said: It is not for God to take any son; glory be to Him (19:35), that is: far above what these ignorant, wrongdoing, transgressing people say, in great exaltation. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it “Be”, and it is (19:35), that is: when He wills a thing, He merely commands it, and it comes to be as He wishes, as He, Exalted, said: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him “Be”, and he was. The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters (3:59–60).

And His words: And surely God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path (19:36), that is: among the things that Jesus commanded his people while he was in his cradle was that he informed them at that very time that God was their Lord and his Lord, and he commanded them to worship Him, saying: so worship Him; this is a straight path (19:36),
that is: this which I have brought you from God is a straight path, that is, an upright one: whoever follows it is rightly guided and well directed, and whoever opposes it goes astray and errs.

And His words: Then the factions differed among themselves (19:37), that is: the statements of the People of the Book concerning Jesus diverged after the exposition of his affair and the clarity of his condition, namely that he is His servant and His messenger and His word which He cast to Mary and a spirit from Him. One party (the generality of the Jews, upon them be the curses of God) resolved that he was a child of fornication, and they said: this speech of his is sorcery. Another party said: it was really God who spoke. Others said: he is the son of God. Others said: the third of three. And others said: rather, he is the servant of God and His messenger. This is the word of truth, to which God guided the believers. Something like this has been related from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, Ibn Jurayj, Qatādah and more than one of the early and the later authorities.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words: That is Jesus son of Mary, the word of truth concerning which they are in doubt (19:34), he said: The Children of Israel assembled and brought forth from among themselves four men, each people bringing forth its learned man, and they disputed about Jesus when he was raised up. One of them said: He is God; He came down to the earth, gave life to whom He gave life and caused to die whom He caused to die, then ascended to heaven, these are the Jacobites. The three said: You have lied. Then two of them said to the third: You speak concerning him. He said: He is the son of God, these are the Nestorians. The two said: You have lied. Then one of the two said to the other: You speak concerning him. He said: He is the third of three: God is a god, he is a god, and his mother is a god, these are the Isrāʾīliyyah{{fn:So the text; other transmissions of this report call this third party the Malkāniyyah (Melkites), the church of the Byzantine emperors, which is clearly what is meant by “the kings of the Christians”.}}, the kings of the Christians, upon them be the curses of God. The fourth said: You have lied; rather, he is the servant of God and His messenger and His spirit and His word, and these are the Muslims. Each man among them had followers upon what they said, and they fought one another, and the Muslims were overcome. That is the saying of God, Exalted: and they kill those among the people who enjoin justice (3:21). Qatādah said: They are the ones of whom God said: Then the factions differed among themselves (19:37); he said: they differed concerning him and became factions.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim has related, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr and from some of the people of knowledge, something close to that. And more than one of the historians, from among the People of the Book and others, has mentioned that Constantine gathered them in a great assembly, one of their three councils famous among them; the company of bishops among them numbered two thousand one hundred and seventy bishops, and they differed concerning Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) with widely divergent differences. Every small band said something about him: a hundred would say one thing about him, seventy would say another thing about him, fifty would say something else about him, and a hundred and sixty would say something; and no more than three hundred and eight of them agreed upon a single statement. These agreed upon a position and held firmly to it, and the king inclined towards them, he was a philosopher, so he advanced them, supported them and drove out all who were other than them. They composed for him the Great Trust{{fn:al-Amānah al-kabīrah, the Muslim historians’ name for the Nicene Creed; Ibn Kathīr puns on amānah (trust) and khiyānah (treachery).}}(nay, it is rather the great treachery) and they composed for him the books of the canons, legislated things for him, innovated many innovations, and distorted the religion of the Messiah and altered it. He then built for them the great churches throughout the whole of his kingdom: the lands of Syria, the Jazīrah and the Byzantine lands, so that the number of churches in his days reached nearly twelve thousand churches. And his mother Helena built the Qumāmah{{fn:Literally “the Dunghill”, the Muslim writers’ deliberate deformation of al-Qiyāmah, the Church of the Resurrection (the Holy Sepulchre) in Jerusalem.}} over the place where the crucified one was crucified, the one whom the Jews and the Christians allege was the Messiah, though they lied; rather, God raised him up to heaven.

And His words: So woe to those who disbelieve from the witnessing of a tremendous Day (19:37): this is a threat and a severe warning to whoever lies against God, forges falsehood and alleges that He has a son. But He, Exalted, has granted them respite until the Day of Resurrection and deferred them, out of forbearance and out of confidence in His power over them, for He is the One who does not hasten against whoever disobeys Him, as has come in the two Ṣaḥīḥs: “Surely God grants respite to the wrongdoer, until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape.” Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recited: And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing; surely His seizing is painful, severe (11:102). In the two Ṣaḥīḥs also it is related from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: “No one is more patient over an injury he hears than God: they attribute a son to Him, while He provides for them and keeps them in health.” And God, Exalted, has said: And how many a town I granted respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the return (22:48). And He, Exalted, said: And do not think that God is heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only defers them to a Day on which the eyes will stare (14:42).

For this reason He said here: So woe to those who disbelieve from the witnessing of a tremendous Day (19:37), that is: the Day of Resurrection. And it has come in the sound ḥadīth, agreed upon as to its soundness, from ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Whoever bears witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His messenger, and that Jesus is the servant of God and His messenger and His word which He cast to Mary and a spirit from Him, and that Paradise is true and the Fire is true, God will admit him to Paradise, whatever his deeds may have been.”

Thus does He, Exalted, join the story of Mary and her son Jesus (peace be upon him) to the story of Zachariah and his son John (peace be upon them both): He first mentions the story of Zachariah and then follows it with the story of Mary, because the former paves the way for the latter. For the former is the bringing into being of a child from an aged old man far advanced in years and from an elderly barren woman who had not borne children in the days of her youth; then He mentions the story of Mary, which is more wondrous still, for it is the bringing into being of a child from a female without a male. So it occurs in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān and in Sūrat Maryam, and here too He mentioned the story of Zachariah and then followed it with the story of Mary. So His words: And she who guarded her chastity (21:91) mean Mary (peace be upon her), as He said in Sūrat al-Taḥrīm: And Mary daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it of Our spirit (66:12).

And His words: and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds (21:91), that is: a proof that God has power over all things and that He creates whatever He wills, and that His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it “Be”, and it is (36:82). This is like His words: and that We may make him a sign for mankind (19:21).

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: My father related to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad related to us, from Shabīb, meaning Ibn Bishr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words: for the worlds (21:91), he said: “the worlds” are the jinn and mankind.

He, Exalted, says, informing about His servant and messenger Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon them both), that He made the two of them a sign for mankind, that is, a decisive proof of His power over whatever He wills: for He created Adam without father or mother, created Eve from a male without a female, created Jesus from a female without a male, and created the rest of mankind from a male and a female.

And His words: and We gave them refuge on a height, a place of rest and flowing water (23:50). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: the “height” (rabwah) is the elevated part of the earth, and it is the best ground for vegetation. So too said Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Qatādah.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: And His words a place of rest (23:50): He says, a place of fertility; and flowing water (23:50) means water visible on the surface.
Mujāhid said: a level height.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: a place of rest and flowing water (23:50): the water lay level upon it. Mujāhid and Qatādah said: and flowing water (23:50): running water.

Then the exegetes differed as to the location of this height: in which of God’s lands is it? ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: There are no heights except in Egypt: when the water is released, the heights are what the villages stand upon, and were it not for the heights the villages would be drowned.
Something like this is related from Wahb ibn Munabbih, and it is very far-fetched.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Muqriʾ related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, concerning His words, Exalted: and We gave them refuge on a height, a place of rest and flowing water (23:50), he said: It is Damascus.
He said: And something like that is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn Aslam and Khālid ibn Maʿdān.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj related to us: Wakīʿ related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: a place of rest and flowing water (23:50), he said: the rivers of Damascus.

Layth ibn Abī Sulaym said, from Mujāhid: and We gave them refuge on a height, a place of rest and flowing water (23:50), he said: Jesus son of Mary and his mother, when they took refuge in the Ghūṭah of Damascus{{fn:The irrigated oasis of orchards surrounding Damascus.}} and its surroundings.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said, from Bishr ibn Rāfiʿ, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the paternal cousin of Abū Hurayrah, who said: I heard Abū Hurayrah say, concerning His words: on a height, a place of rest and flowing water (23:50), he said: It is Ramlah in Palestine.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: My father related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-Firyābī related to us: Rawwād ibn al-Jarrāḥ related to us: ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād al-Khawwāṣ Abū ʿUtbah related to us: al-Saybānī related to us, from Ibn Waʿlah, from Kurayb al-Saḥūlī, from Murrah al-Bahzī, who said: I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say to a man: “You will die at the height (al-rabwah)”, and he died at Ramlah. This is a very strange (gharīb) ḥadīth.

The nearest of the opinions on this is what al-ʿAwfī related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words: and We gave them refuge on a height, a place of rest and flowing water (23:50), he said: the “flowing water” (maʿīn) is running water, and it is the stream of which God, Exalted, said: Your Lord has placed beneath you a rivulet (19:24).

So too said al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatādah: on a height, a place of rest and flowing water (23:50): it is Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). This, and God knows best, is the most evident view, because it is what is mentioned in the other verse; and the Qurʾan explains one part of itself by another. That is the most fitting means by which it is to be explained, then the sound ḥadīths, then the transmitted reports (āthār).

He, Exalted, says, informing of the obstinacy of Quraysh in their disbelief and their deliberate stubbornness and disputation: And when the son of Mary was put forth as an example, behold, your people cry out at it (43:57). More than one has said, from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī: they laugh, that is, they were delighted by that.
Qatādah said: they are perturbed and they laugh. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: they turn away.

The reason for that was what Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq mentioned in the Sīrah, where he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sat one day, according to what has reached me, with al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah in the mosque, and al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith came and sat with them, there being in the gathering more than one of the men of Quraysh. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) spoke, and al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith confronted him, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) spoke with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them: Surely you and what you worship apart from God are the fuel of Hell; to it you shall come down (21:98) and the verses following. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) rose, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā al-Tamīmī came forward and sat down, and al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah said to him: By God, al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith could neither stand up to the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib nor hold his seat{{fn:An idiom: he was altogether unable to cope with him.}}; and Muḥammad has claimed that we and what we worship of these gods of ours are the fuel of Hell. ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā said: Now by God, had I found him I would have bested him in argument. Ask Muḥammad: is everything that is worshipped apart from God in Hell together with those who worshipped it? For we worship the angels, the Jews worship ʿUzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah Jesus son of Mary. Al-Walīd and those who were with him in the gathering marvelled at the words of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā, and they considered that he had argued and disputed well. That was mentioned to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and he said: “Everyone who loves to be worshipped apart from God is with those who worshipped him; for they are only worshipping Satan and whoever commanded them to worship him.” So God, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: Surely those for whom the best has already gone forth from Us, they shall be kept far from it (21:101), that is: Jesus, ʿUzayr and those who were worshipped along with them of the rabbis and monks who passed away in obedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, whom the people of error who worshipped them took as lords apart from God. And there came down, concerning what they mention of their worshipping the angels and that they are the daughters of God: And they say: The Most Merciful has taken a son. Glory be to Him! Nay, they are honoured servants (21:26) and the verses following. And there came down, concerning what is mentioned of the affair of Jesus and that he is worshipped apart from God, and the marvelling of al-Walīd and those present with him at his argument and his disputation: And when the son of Mary was put forth as an example, behold, your people cry out at it (43:57), that is: they turn away from your affair on account of that saying of his. Then He mentioned Jesus and said: He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And had We willed, We could have made of you angels in the earth to succeed. And surely he is a knowledge of the Hour (43:59–61), that is: what I placed in his hands of signs, the reviving of the dead and the curing of illnesses, suffices as a proof of the knowledge of the Hour. He says: so do not doubt concerning it, and follow me; this is a straight path (43:61).

Ibn Jarīr mentioned, from the transmission of al-ʿAwfī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, His words: And when the son of Mary was put forth as an example, behold, your people cry out at it (43:57), he said: meaning Quraysh; when it was said to them: Surely you and what you worship apart from God are the fuel of Hell; to it you shall come down (21:98), to the end of the verses, Quraysh said to him: Then what of the son of Mary? He said: “That one is the servant of God and His messenger.” They said: By God, this man wants nothing but that we take him as a lord, as the Christians took Jesus son of Mary as a lord. So God, Exalted, said: They did not put it forth to you except for argument; nay, they are a contentious people (43:58).

Imām Aḥmad said: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim related to us: Shaybān related to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Abū Razīn, from Abū Yaḥyā, the client of Ibn ʿAqīl al-Anṣārī, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I know a verse of the Qurʾan about which no man has ever asked me, and I do not know whether people know it and so have not asked about it, or whether they have not noticed it so as to ask about it. He said: Then he began to relate to us, and when he rose we blamed one another for not having asked him about it. I said: I shall see to it when he comes tomorrow. When the next day came I said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, you mentioned yesterday that there is a verse of the Qurʾan about which no man has ever asked you, and that you do not know whether people know it or have not noticed it. And I said: Tell me about it, and about those verses you recited before it. He said: Yes. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Quraysh: “O company of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped apart from God in whom there is any good.” Now Quraysh knew that the Christians worship Jesus son of Mary, and what they say about Muḥammad, so they said: O Muḥammad, do you not claim that Jesus was a prophet and a righteous servant among the servants of God? If you are truthful, then their gods are as you people say. He said: So God sent down: And when the son of Mary was put forth as an example, behold, your people cry out at it (43:57). I said: What is “yaṣiddūn”? He said: They laugh. And surely he is a knowledge of the Hour (43:61), he said: it is the coming forth of Jesus son of Mary before the Resurrection.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Dimashqī related to us: Ādam related to us: Shaybān related to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Abū Aḥmad, the client of the Anṣār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “O company of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped apart from God in whom there is any good.” They said to him: Do you not claim that Jesus was a prophet and a righteous servant among the servants of God? Yet he has been worshipped apart from God. So God, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: And when the son of Mary was put forth as an example, behold, your people cry out at it (43:57).

Mujāhid said concerning His words: And when the son of Mary was put forth as an example, behold, your people cry out at it (43:57): Quraysh said: Muḥammad only wants us to worship him as the people of Jesus worshipped Jesus. Qatādah said something similar to this.

And His words: And they say: Are our gods better, or he? (43:58). Qatādah said: they say, our gods are better than he. And Qatādah said: Ibn Masʿūd read: “And they say: Are our gods better, or this one?”, meaning Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).

And His words: They did not put it forth to you except for argument (43:58), that is: for wrangling, while they knew that it did not apply to the verse, because the verse concerns what has no intelligence, namely His words: Surely you and what you worship apart from God are the fuel of Hell (21:98). Also, it is an address to Quraysh, and they used to worship only idols and rivals set up beside God; they did not worship the Messiah, so that they might adduce him. Thus it is established that their statement was only disputation on their part, of whose correctness they themselves were not convinced.

Imām Aḥmad (may God, Exalted, have mercy on him) said: Ibn Numayr related to us: Ḥajjāj ibn Dīnār related to us, from Abū Ghālib, from Abū Umāmah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “No people ever went astray after guidance they were upon except that they were given to disputation.” Then he recited this verse: They did not put it forth to you except for argument; nay, they are a contentious people (43:58).
Al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah and Ibn Jarīr have related it from the ḥadīth of Ḥajjāj ibn Dīnār, with this chain. Then al-Tirmidhī said: ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ; we know it only from his ḥadīth. So he said.

It has been related by another route from Abū Umāmah with an addition. Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAyyāsh al-Ramlī related to us: Muʾammal related to us: Ḥammād related to us: Ibn Makhzūm informed us, from al-Qāsim Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Shāmī, from Abū Umāmah (Ḥammād said: I do not know whether he traced it back to the Prophet or not) who said: No community went astray after its prophet except that the first of its going astray was the denial of the divine decree (qadar); and no community went astray after its prophet except that they were given to disputation. Then he recited: They did not put it forth to you except for argument; nay, they are a contentious people (43:58).

Ibn Jarīr also said: Abū Kurayb related to us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, from ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād, from Jaʿfar, from al-Qāsim, from Abū Umāmah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came out to the people while they were disputing about the Qurʾan, and he became exceedingly angry, until it was as if vinegar had been poured over his face; then he said: “Do not strike one part of the Book of God against another, for no people ever went astray except that they were given to disputation.” Then he recited: They did not put it forth to you except for argument; nay, they are a contentious people (43:58).

And His words: He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour (43:59), meaning Jesus (peace be upon him): he is nothing but a servant among the servants of God, upon whom God bestowed the favour of prophethood and messengership; and We made him an example for the Children of Israel (43:59), that is: a sign, an argument and a proof of Our power over whatever We will.

And His words: And had We willed, We could have made of you (43:60), that is: in your place, angels in the earth to succeed (43:60). Al-Suddī said: to succeed you in it. Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah said: succeeding one another, as you succeed one another. This view entails the first. Mujāhid said: populating the earth in your stead.

And His words: And surely he is a knowledge of the Hour (43:61): the interpretation of Ibn Isḥāq has already been given, that what is meant by it is that with which Jesus (peace be upon him) was sent, of reviving the dead and curing the one born blind and the leper and other illnesses. This is open to question. Further from the mark than this is what Qatādah reported from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, namely that the pronoun in and surely he refers to the Qurʾan. Rather, the correct view is that it refers to Jesus (peace be upon him), for the context is concerned with mentioning him; and then what is meant by it is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as He, Blessed and Exalted, said: And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death, that is, before the death of Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him), then and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them (4:159). This meaning is supported by the other reading: “wa-innahu la-ʿalamun li-l-sāʿah”{{fn:Reading ʿalam (“token, landmark”) in place of ʿilm (“knowledge”); it is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatādah and others.}}, that is: a token and a proof of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujāhid said: And surely he is a knowledge of the Hour (43:61), that is: a sign of the Hour is the coming forth of Jesus son of Mary before the Day of Resurrection. So too has it been related from Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, Abū Mālik, ʿIkrimah, al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others.

The ḥadīths from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) have come down by multiple concurrent transmission (tawātur) that he foretold the descent of Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) before the Day of Resurrection as a just leader and an equitable judge.

And His words: so do not doubt concerning it (43:61), that is: do not be in doubt about it; it will come to pass and happen without fail; and follow me (43:61), that is: in what I inform you of; this is a straight path. And let not Satan hinder you (43:61–62), that is: from following the truth; surely he is to you a manifest enemy. And when Jesus came with the clear proofs, he said: I have come to you with wisdom (43:62–63), that is: with prophethood, and that I may make clear to you some of that wherein you differ (43:63).

Ibn Jarīr said: meaning of religious matters, not worldly ones. What he has said is good and sound. He then refuted the view of those who claimed that “some” (baʿḍ) here has the sense of “all”, and who adduced as evidence the verse of the poet Labīd:
> Forsaking places when I am not pleased with them,
> or else death fastens upon some souls and takes them.
They interpreted it as meaning that he intended all souls. Ibn Jarīr said: He intended only his own soul, and expressed it by “some”. What he has said is possible.

And His words: So fear God (43:63), that is: in what He has commanded you, and obey me (43:63), in what I have brought you; Surely God, He is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path (43:64), that is: I and you are servants of His, in need of Him, sharing together in the worship of Him alone, who has no partner; this is a straight path (43:64), that is: this which I have brought you is the straight path, namely the worship of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, alone.

And His words: Then the factions differed among themselves (43:65), that is: the sects differed and became divided parties concerning him: among them are those who acknowledge that he is the servant of God and His messenger (and that is the truth; among them are those who claim that he is the son of God; and among them are those who say that he is God) exalted be God above their saying in great exaltation. For this reason He said: So woe to those who do wrong from the punishment of a painful Day (43:65).

He, Exalted, informs that since He sent Noah (peace be upon him) He has not sent after him any messenger or prophet except from his progeny; and likewise Abraham (peace be upon him), the Intimate Friend of the Most Merciful: He has not sent down from heaven any scripture, nor sent any messenger, nor revealed to any human being after him, except that he was of his lineage, as He said in the other verse: and We placed among their progeny prophethood and the Scripture (57:26), meaning, until the last of the prophets of the Children of Israel was Jesus son of Mary, who gave glad tidings after him of Muḥammad (the blessings and peace of God be upon them both). For this reason He, Exalted, said: Then We sent Our messengers to follow in their footsteps, and We sent Jesus son of Mary to follow, and We gave him the Gospel (57:27),

which is the Book that God revealed to him; and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him (57:27), and they are the disciples, compassion and mercy (57:27), that is: compassion (raʾfah), which is reverent fear, and mercy (57:27) towards creation.

And His words: and monasticism which they invented (57:27), that is: the community of the Christians invented it; We did not prescribe it for them (57:27), that is: We did not legislate it for them; rather, they bound themselves to it of their own accord.
And His words: except seeking the good pleasure of God (57:27): on this there are two views.
- One of them: that they intended by that the good pleasure of God; so said Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Qatādah.
- The other: We did not prescribe that for them; We prescribed for them only the seeking of the good pleasure of God.

And His words: but they did not observe it with its due observance (57:27), that is: they did not fulfil what they had bound themselves to as it ought to be fulfilled. This is a censure of them from two aspects:
- the first, for innovating in the religion of God what God did not command;
- and the second, for their failure to fulfil what they had bound themselves to, of what they alleged to be an act of devotion bringing them near to God, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Isḥāq ibn Abī Ḥamzah Abū Yaʿqūb al-Rāzī related to us: al-Sindī ibn ʿAbdawayh related to us: Bukayr ibn Maʿrūf related to us, from Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from his father, from his grandfather Ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: “O Ibn Masʿūd.” I said: At your service, O Messenger of God. He said: “Do you know that the Children of Israel split into seventy-two sects, of which none were saved but three sects? One stood up among the kings and the tyrants after Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) and called to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus son of Mary; it fought the tyrants and was slain, and it endured patiently and was saved. Then another group stood up which had no strength for fighting; it stood up among the kings and the tyrants and they called to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus son of Mary, and it was slain and sawn asunder with saws and burnt with fire, and it endured patiently and was saved. Then another group stood up which had no strength for fighting and was not able to uphold justice, so it took to the mountains and devoted itself to worship and became monks; and these are the ones whom God, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned: and monasticism which they invented; We did not prescribe it for them (57:27).”

Ibn Jarīr related it with another wording by another route, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Ṭālib related to us: Dāwūd ibn al-Muḥabbar related to us: al-Ṣaʿq ibn Ḥazn related to us: ʿUqayl al-Jaʿdī related to us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Those who were before us split into seventy-three sects; three of them were saved and the rest of them perished…”, and he mentioned the like of what has preceded, and in it: “So We gave those of them who believed their reward (57:27): they are the ones who believed in me and affirmed me; but many of them are transgressors (57:27): they are the ones who denied me and opposed me.”

The condition of Dāwūd ibn al-Muḥabbar, for he is one of the fabricators of ḥadīth, does not impair this corroborating transmission (mutābaʿah), since Abū Yaʿlā has also transmitted it with a chain of his own, from Shaybān ibn Farrūkh, from al-Ṣaʿq ibn Ḥazn, with the like of that; and so the ḥadīth is strengthened by this route.

Ibn Jarīr and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Nasāʾī, the wording being his, said: al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥurayth informed us: al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā related to us, from Sufyān ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both), who said: There were kings after Jesus (peace be upon him) who altered the Torah and the Gospel, and among the people were believers who used to recite the Torah and the Gospel. It was said to their kings: We find nothing more severe than the abuse with which these people abuse us: they recite: And whoever does not judge by what God has sent down, those are the disbelievers (5:44), these verses, together with what they reproach us with concerning our deeds in their recitation; so summon them and let them recite as we recite and believe as we believe. So he summoned them and gathered them together and offered them death, or else that they abandon the recitation of the Torah and the Gospel, except what they had altered of them. They said: What do you want with that? Leave us be. One group of them said: Build us a pillar, then raise us up onto it, then give us something by which we may hoist up our food and drink, and we shall not trouble you. Another group said: Leave us to wander in the earth and roam and drink as the wild beasts drink, and if you catch us in your land, then kill us. Another group said: Build us houses in the deserts, and we shall dig wells and cultivate vegetables, and we shall not trouble you nor pass by you. And there was no tribe but had a close kinsman among them, so they did that; and God, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: and monasticism which they invented; We did not prescribe it for them, except seeking the good pleasure of God; but they did not observe it with its due observance (57:27). The others said: We shall worship as So-and-so worshipped, wander as So-and-so wandered, and take houses as So-and-so took houses, while they were upon their polytheism, having no knowledge of the faith of those whom they imitated. When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent and only a few of them remained, a man came down from his hermitage, a wanderer came from his wandering and the master of a monastery from his monastery, and they believed in him and affirmed him. So God, Mighty and Majestic, said: O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy (57:28): two rewards, for their belief in Jesus son of Mary, the Torah and the Gospel, and for their belief in Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and their affirmation of him. He said: and He will appoint for you a light by which you shall walk (57:28): the Qurʾan and their following of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). He said: so that the People of the Book may know (57:29), those who imitate you, that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God, and that bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty (57:29).
This narrative contains some strangeness, and the interpretation of these latter two verses will come in a manner other than this; and God knows best.

The Ḥāfiẓ Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī said: Aḥmad ibn ʿĪsā related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb related to us: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-ʿAmyāʾ related to me that Sahl ibn Abī Umāmah related to him that he and his father went in to Anas ibn Mālik in Medina in the time of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, when he was governor, and he was praying a light prayer, as though it were the prayer of a traveller or close to it. When he gave the salutation, he said: May God have mercy on you; do you consider this prayer to be the prescribed prayer, or something supererogatory you have performed? He said: It is the prescribed prayer, and it is the prayer of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him); I have not erred except in something I have forgotten. For the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: “Do not be severe with yourselves, lest severity be shown to you; for a people were severe with themselves and severity was shown to them, and those are their remnants in the hermitages and the monasteries: ‘monasticism which they invented; We did not prescribe it for them’.” Then they set out the next morning and said: Let us ride and look and take a lesson. He said: Yes. So they all rode, and behold, they came upon desolate dwellings whose people had perished, died out and passed away, fallen in upon their roofs. They said: Do you know these dwellings? He said: How well I know them and their people! These are the people of these dwellings; oppression and envy destroyed them. Surely envy extinguishes the light of good deeds, and oppression confirms that or belies it; and the eye commits fornication, and the hand, the foot, the body and the tongue, and the private parts confirm that or belie it.

Imām Aḥmad said: Yaʿmar related to us: ʿAbd Allāh related to us: Sufyān informed us, from Zayd al-ʿAmmī, from Abū Iyās, from Anas ibn Mālik, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Every prophet has a monasticism, and the monasticism of this community is striving (jihād) in the way of God, Mighty and Majestic.”

The Ḥāfiẓ Abū Yaʿlā related it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Asmāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak, with this chain, and its wording is: “Every community has a monasticism, and the monasticism of this community is striving in the way of God.”

Imām Aḥmad said: Ḥusayn (that is, Ibn Muḥammad) related to us: Ibn ʿAyyāsh, meaning Ismāʿīl, related to us, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn Marwān al-Kalāʿī and ʿUqayl ibn Mudrik al-Sulamī, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may God be pleased with him), that a man came to him and said: Counsel me. He said: You have asked about what I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) before you. I counsel you to fear God, for it is the head of everything; and hold fast to striving (jihād), for it is the monasticism of Islam; and hold fast to the remembrance of God and the recitation of the Qurʾan, for it is your spirit in heaven and your mention on the earth. Aḥmad alone has related it.

God, Exalted, says, informing of His servant and messenger, the one to whom He spoke, Moses son of ʿImrān (peace be upon him), that he said to his people: Why do you harm me, when you know well that I am the messenger of God to you? (61:5), that is: why do you direct harm at me when you know my truthfulness in the message I have brought you? In this there is consolation for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) in what befell him from the unbelievers of his people and others, and a command to him to be patient. For this reason he said: "May the mercy of God be upon Moses: he was harmed with more than this, and he bore it patiently." In it there is also a prohibition to the believers against assailing the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) or directing any harm at him, as He, Exalted, said: O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Moses, and God cleared him of what they said, and he was honourable in the sight of God (33:69).

And His words: So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate (61:5), that is: when they turned aside from following the truth despite their knowledge of it, God caused their hearts to deviate from guidance and lodged in them doubt, bewilderment and abandonment, as He, Exalted, said: And We shall turn about their hearts and their eyes, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We shall leave them in their transgression wandering blindly (6:110), and He said: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers, We shall turn him to what he has turned to and roast him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination (4:115). For this reason God, Exalted, said in this verse: and God does not guide the people who are defiantly disobedient (61:5).

And His words: And when Jesus son of Mary said: O Children of Israel, truly I am the messenger of God to you, confirming what was before me of the Torah, and bringing glad tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Aḥmad (61:6), meaning: the Torah has given glad tidings of me, and I am the fulfilment of what it foretold, and I bring glad tidings of the one who comes after me, who is the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, the Arab, the Meccan, Aḥmad. So Jesus (peace be upon him), who is the seal of the prophets of the Children of Israel, stood up among the assembly of the Children of Israel giving glad tidings of Muḥammad, who is Aḥmad, the seal of the prophets and messengers, after whom there is no message and no prophethood. How excellent is what al-Bukhārī has cited, the ḥadīth in which he said:

Abū al-Yamān related to us: Shuʿayb related to us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim informed me, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "I have names: I am Muḥammad, and I am Aḥmad, and I am al-Māḥī (the Effacer), by whom God effaces unbelief, and I am al-Ḥāshir (the Gatherer), at whose feet mankind will be gathered, and I am al-ʿĀqib (the Last)."
Muslim related it from the ḥadīth of al-Zuhrī, with this chain, in similar terms.

Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī said: al-Masʿūdī related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Abū Mūsā, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) named for us several names of his, some of which we have retained; he said: "I am Muḥammad, and I am Aḥmad, and al-Ḥāshir (the Gatherer), and al-Muqaffī (the One who comes last in the succession), and the Prophet of mercy, and of repentance, and of the final battle (malḥamah)."

Muslim related it from the ḥadīth of al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, with this chain. And God, Exalted, has said: those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel (7:157), and He, Exalted, said: And when God took the covenant of the prophets: Whatever I give you of Book and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him and surely support him. He said: Do you affirm, and take upon yourselves My burden on that? They said: We affirm. He said: Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses (3:81).

Ibn ʿAbbās said: God did not send any prophet without taking from him the pledge that if Muḥammad were sent while he was alive, he would surely follow him; and He took from him that he should take the pledge from his community that if Muḥammad were sent while they were alive, they would surely follow him and support him.

Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: Thawr ibn Yazīd related to me, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), that they said: O Messenger of God, tell us about yourself. He said: "The supplication of my father Abraham, and the glad tidings of Jesus; and my mother saw, when she conceived me, as though a light went forth from her by which the palaces of Buṣrā{{fn:Bostra, in the Ḥawrān, south of Damascus.}} in the land of Syria were lit up."
This is a good chain of transmission (isnād). Corroborating reports (shawāhid) for it have been related by other routes. The Imām Aḥmad said:

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Suwayd al-Kalbī, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Hilāl al-Sulamī, from al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Truly, with God I was the Seal of the Prophets while Adam was still cast in his clay. And I shall tell you of the first of that: the supplication of my father Abraham, and the glad tidings of Jesus concerning me, and the vision of my mother which she saw; and likewise do the mothers of the prophets see."

Aḥmad also said: Abū al-Naḍr related to us: al-Faraj ibn Faḍālah related to us: Luqmān ibn ʿĀmir related to us, who said: I heard Abū Umāmah say: I said: O Prophet of God, what was the beginning of your affair? He said: "The supplication of my father Abraham, and the glad tidings of Jesus; and my mother saw that a light went forth from her by which the palaces of Syria were lit up."

Aḥmad also said: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā related to us: I heard Khudayj, the brother of Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sent us to the Negus, and we were about eighty men, among them ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Jaʿfar, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUrfuṭah, ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn and Abū Mūsā. They came to the Negus; and Quraysh sent ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and ʿUmārah ibn al-Walīd with a gift. When the two of them entered upon the Negus they prostrated to him, then hastened to take their places on his right and on his left, then said to him: "Some men of our cousins have settled in your land, having turned away from us and from our religion." He said: "And where are they?" They said: "They are in your land, so send for them." So he sent for them. Jaʿfar said: "I shall be your spokesman today." So they followed him, and he gave the greeting of peace and did not prostrate. They said to him: "What is the matter with you, that you do not prostrate to the king?" He said: "We prostrate to none but God, Mighty and Majestic." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "God has sent His messenger to us, and he has commanded us not to prostrate to anyone but God, Mighty and Majestic, and he has commanded us to prayer and alms."

ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: "But they differ from you concerning Jesus son of Mary." He said: "What do you say about Jesus son of Mary and his mother?" They said: "We say as God, Mighty and Majestic, has said: he is the word of God and His spirit, which He cast to the virgin, the chaste one (al-batūl), whom no man had touched and to whom no child had ever come." He said: Then he lifted a stick from the ground and said: "O company of Abyssinians, priests and monks! By God, they do not add to what we say about him so much as the measure of this. Welcome to you, and to him from whom you have come. I bear witness that he is the messenger of God, and that he is the one we find in the Gospel, and that he is the one of whom Jesus son of Mary gave glad tidings. Settle wherever you wish. By God, were it not for the kingship I am engaged in, I would go to him, so that I might be the one to carry his sandals and pour the water for his ablutions." And he ordered that the gift of the other two be returned to them. Then ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd hurried back, so that he was present at Badr; and he maintained that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) asked forgiveness for him{{fn:For the Negus.}} when news of his death reached him.

This story has been related from Jaʿfar and from Umm Salamah (may God be pleased with them both), and its proper place is the Book of the Sīrah. The point is that the prophets (peace be upon them) never ceased to describe him and tell of him in their scriptures to their communities, commanding them to follow him, support him and assist him when he was sent. What was most widely known of the matter among the people of the earth was on the tongue of Abraham the Friend (al-Khalīl), the father of the prophets after him, when he prayed for the people of Mecca that God would send among them a messenger from among themselves, and likewise on the tongue of Jesus son of Mary. For this reason they said: "Tell us about the beginning of your affair," meaning, on the earth; and he said: "The supplication of my father Abraham, and the glad tidings of Jesus son of Mary, and the vision of my mother which she saw," that is: the trace of that, and the foreshadowing (irhāṣ) by the mention of him, appeared among the people of Mecca (God's blessings and peace be upon him).

And His words: But when he came to them with the clear proofs, they said: This is manifest sorcery (61:6). Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Jarīr said: But when he came to them (Aḥmad, that is, the one of whom glad tidings were given in the ancient ages, whose mention was proclaimed in the bygone generations) when his affair appeared and he came with the clear proofs, the unbelievers and the opponents said: This is manifest sorcery.
